topPRs.title: fix(voice): wire the realtime voice client into the chat UI + staging deploy flag (closes the app-staging bundle gap)
topPRs.author: 0xSolace
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Realtime voice Phase-1 staging rollout. Follow-up to #16062 (server + client library) and #16105. Root cause + evidence: `VOICE-UI-STAGING-GAP-REPORT.md` (fleet workspace).

Definition of Done: full standard in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

- [x] This PR targets `develop` and is rebased onto the latest `origin/develop` (c93ebbb73c3) with zero conflicts.
- [x] `bun install` run after sync; targeted typecheck + unit suites pass (see Testing).
- [x] A reviewer can confirm the change works without reading the code, from the evidence attached below.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Built directly on `origin/develop` @ c93ebbb73c3; all six cherry-picks applied clean.
- [x] Targeted verify (ui typecheck, cloud/api voice tests, biome) passes post-sync.

# Risks

**Low-medium.**
- UI: the realtime path is dead code unless `VITE_VOICE_REALTIME_WS=1` is baked at build time AND the server mint succeeds. Production builds keep the flag at `0`, so prod behavior is byte-identical on the voice path.
- Workflow: `.github/workflows/cloud-cf-deploy.yml` changes (staging-only voice env plumbing + `VITE_VOICE_REALTIME_WS` gated to `0` on production/main). **Workflow-file change: flagged for orchestrator review per fleet law.**
- Worker: `wrangler.toml` staging vars for the voice session service (staging section only) + a `binaryType` fix in the WS route that only executes when the voice WS feature flag is on.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Closes the staging gap where api-staging has the realtime voice server live (mint/consent/WS routes answering 200) but the app-staging bundle contains **no client path to reach it**. #16062 merged the voice-session client *library* (`packages/ui/src/voice/voice-session-*`) but not the chat-UI wiring, so nothing in the develop-built bundle imports `createVoiceSessionClient`, and the deploy workflow never set the build-time flag.

Six commits cherry-picked from `feat/voice-standalone-backend` (the branch behind the working 2026-07-10 staging build), plus one rebase-hygiene commit:

1. `50d27a94acf` feat(ui): wire realtime voice-session client into the existing chat mic UI — `useRealtimeVoiceSession` / `useRealtimeVoiceMint` / `useContinuousVoiceSession` hooks + ChatView/chat-view-hooks integration. Realtime is an ADDITIVE enhancement of the existing continuous-mic toggle; batch path unchanged when unavailable.
2. `fbc40396a27` fix(ui): route forced realtime voice through mic controls.
3. `1065f619b3e` feat(voice): force-arm override (`VITE_VOICE_REALTIME_FORCE`, default OFF everywhere; set to "0" explicitly in the workflow).
4. `f0b9708743b` chore(cloud): enable realtime voice on staging deploy — workflow secrets plumbing + staging wrangler vars + `VITE_VOICE_REALTIME_WS` = 1 on staging, 0 on production/main.
5. `549b8c8890d` fix(cloud): staging voice auth fallback (dedicated secrets preferred, ElizaCloud API key fallback so the Worker is not deployed half-configured).
6. `c4aa4eeffa8` fix(cloud): set voice WS server `binaryType` to arraybuffer so audio uplink works.
7. `731ab66cda0` fix(ui): biome format + drop an unused `continuous` destructure that the develop rebase made dead.

## What kind of change is this?

Features (staging-gated) + fixes.

# Documentation changes needed?

`packages/ui/src/voice/REALTIME_VOICE_UI_WIRING.md` ships in this PR (wiring contract + manual test script).

# Testing

**Build-time flag proof (the actual bug):** staging-config app build from this branch (`VITE_VOICE_REALTIME_WS=1 VITE_ENVIRONMENT=staging bun run build` in `packages/app`) produces a bundle where:
- `createVoiceSessionClient` is present in the chat chunk (`src-*.js`, `voice-*.js`)
- the main chunk carries `VITE_VOICE_REALTIME_WS:"1"` and the consent-route reference `voice/session/consent`

Current staging bundle (built from develop without this PR) has ZERO of these; verified by downloading all 177 chunks of `app-staging.elizacloud.ai` and grepping.

**Unit:** `packages/ui` — useRealtimeVoiceSession (18), useRealtimeVoiceMint (12), useContinuousVoiceSession (7), chat-view-hooks (5), ChatVoiceStatusBar (8), BackgroundView (6): **56/56 pass**.
`packages/cloud/api` — ws-route-upgrade + ws-lifecycle + mint-consent-route: **27/27 pass** (bun test).

**Types:** `packages/ui` tsgo --noEmit clean. `packages/cloud/api` typecheck clean (wrangler dry-run completes).

**Lint:** biome clean on all touched files.

**Server side already live on staging:** POST `/api/v1/voice/session/consent` returns 200 + consentNonce with `VOICE_REALTIME_WS_ENABLED=true` (restored as worker secret 2026-07-12).

# Deploy notes

- Staging Pages deploy will bake `VITE_VOICE_REALTIME_WS=1` → realtime arms only after a successful server mint; falls back to batch otherwise.
- Production/main builds evaluate the same expression to `0` → no behavior change.
- Rollback = revert this PR or flip the workflow env to `0`.

[sol-cloud]

topPRs.title: feat(ui): account command-center table
topPRs.author: 0xSolace
topPRs.body:
## What & why

Next slice of the account-observability roadmap (after #16355). Users running a large credential pool get a proper **command-center table** instead of a stack of cards, so health, usage, resets, priority, and lease activity are legible at a glance and sortable.

Renders as a **desktop enhancement** (`min-width:1024px`, the same query `SettingsView` uses for the settings rail from #16354) once a provider pool has **>= 4 accounts**. Narrow/mobile widths and small pools keep the existing `AccountCard` stack (which carries the richer per-card affordances). The card view is untouched.

### Columns
account (label + email) · **health** badge (ok / needs-reauth / rate-limited / invalid, with `healthDetail` tooltip + rate-limit countdown) · session/weekly **usage** bars · **resets** (relative) · **priority** · **enabled** toggle · **last-used** (relative) · **leases** (feature-gated, see below) · **actions**.

### Row states & actions
- **Sortable** by health / usage / last-used / priority. Default surfaces worst health first (the reason to open the table). `aria-sort` lives on the header `<th>` cell.
- **needs-reauth / invalid** → a repair CTA that reuses the **existing #16314 credential-repair flow** (`replaceAccountId` path via `onReauthenticate`).
- **rate-limited** → a live "resets in …" countdown in the health cell.
- **disabled** rows are dimmed.
- Full card affordance parity preserved in the actions cell: **test**, **refresh usage**, **reorder** (priority up/down — targets the priority neighbour regardless of the current table sort), reauthenticate, and remove (confirm dialog). Every row action is an optional prop and hides when its handler is absent.
- Loading is upstream (the table only mounts with data). Empty/degenerate pool → an in-table empty row; the surface's overall empty state remains the existing add-account CTA in `AccountManagementPanel`.

### Feature-detection (does NOT depend on #16355 merging)
#16355 adds an `observability` field (`activeLeaseCount`, `lastLeaseAt`, `lastSelectedAt`, `servedLastRequest`) to each account. This PR feature-detects it: the **Leases column is hidden entirely** when no row carries observability, so it degrades gracefully on older hosts and pre-#16355 payloads — no column of lying zeros, no crash. The client types are augmented with the **optional** shape only.

### Design gate (#16367)
packages/ui tokens + lucide-react only, **no new deps**. The new files introduce **zero** `no-focus-ring-gate` / `no-widget-chrome-gate` offenders (verified against the source-scanning suites; the only account-surface offenders on `develop` are the pre-existing ones #16367 already targets, none in the new files).

## Verification

- `vitest run src/components/accounts/account-table-model.test.ts` → **16 passed** (health mapping, usage extraction, sort comparators incl. unknown-usage sink in both directions, `hasLeaseObservability` feature-detection, `rowResetAt`).
- `vitest run src/components/accounts/AccountCommandTable.test.tsx` → **14 passed** (renders rows, default worst-health sort, header-click sort toggle, health→badge tone mapping, lease-column hide/show, reauth CTA gating + wiring, disabled-row dimming + enabled toggle, test/refresh/reorder wiring + priority-neighbour targeting + disabled edges, `aria-sort` on `<th>`, active-row + empty state).
- Full `src/components/accounts/` suite → **118 passed / 14 files**, no regressions (stories-smoke 33→36).
- `tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → no errors in changed files (the only two are the pre-existing unbuilt `@elizaos/cloud-routing` dep in `packages/core`).

## Evidence

Desktop screenshots captured at 1440px (matching the rail breakpoint) from the built storybook bundle via headless chromium: the table with #16355 observability (leases column + "served last" marker), without observability (leases column absent — feature-detection proven), the empty pool, and a scrolled desktop-slice proving the table body scrolls while the surrounding layout holds.

Media upload to the shared `pr-evidence` release is blocked repo-wide by GitHub's 1000/1000-asset hard cap (same block #16367 documents). Rows are marked honestly below; the PNGs are staged locally and will be attached once a maintainer prunes that release.

<!-- evidence-row:before-screenshots -->
- [ ] Before screenshots — N/A: new component, no prior table state; the pre-existing card view is unchanged and still covered by its own stories/tests.
<!-- evidence-row:after-screenshots -->
- [ ] After screenshots — desktop 1440px renders of with-observability / without-observability / empty-pool captured from the storybook bundle; DOM-verified (5 rows each with Test/Refresh/reorder, `aria-sort=ascending` on the Health `<th>`, Leases column present only with observability). Media upload blocked by the full `pr-evidence` release.
<!-- evidence-row:walkthrough-video -->
- [ ] Walkthrough video — N/A: static table surface; sort/action behavior is proven by the vitest suite. Desktop-scroll-slice screenshot staged to prove content scrolls.
<!-- evidence-row:backend-logs -->
- [ ] Backend logs — N/A: renderer-only change; consumes existing `/api/accounts/*` payloads, no backend path touched.
<!-- evidence-row:frontend-logs -->
- [ ] Frontend logs — N/A: no new network behavior; the table is a projection of already-fetched `useAccounts` data.
<!-- evidence-row:llm-trajectory -->
- [ ] Real-LLM trajectory — N/A: no agent/action/provider/prompt/model change.
<!-- evidence-row:domain-artifacts -->
- [ ] Domain artifacts — N/A: UI-only change, no domain artifacts produced.

---

Auto-merge intentionally NOT armed (auth-adjacent surface).

topPRs.title: feat(orchestrator): add gated lane planner (W1 of #16443)
topPRs.author: 0xSolace
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

W1 of #16443.

Definition of Done: full standard in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

- [x] This PR targets `develop` and is rebased onto the latest `origin/develop` with zero conflicts.
- [ ] `bun install` and `bun run verify` were run after sync. The exact unrelated local dependency/typecheck blockers are recorded below.

# Sync with develop

- [ ] `bun run verify` passes post-sync. Local workspace dependency blockers are documented under **Known gaps / failures**.

# Risks

Low to medium. The integration is default OFF behind `ELIZA_ORCHESTRATOR_LANE_PLANNER`. When disabled, `TASKS create` immediately uses the unchanged legacy path. When enabled, only create requests with explicit, mutually exclusive scoped subtasks become concurrent lane task runs. Planning and collision-discovery failures degrade to the legacy path before execution starts.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Adds W1's `LanePlannerService` to `plugin-agent-orchestrator`:

- pure deterministic decomposition and overlap rejection
- structured `LaneSpec` values with scope, forbidden paths, open-PR/sibling collision annotations, routing-compatible difficulty tag, acceptance criteria seed, and initial prompt
- sibling scope unioning into every lane's forbidden paths
- optional defensive `TEXT_SMALL` refinement behind a separate setting
- one minted wave id stamped into ACP session and durable task metadata
- one existing `runCreateLegacy`/Smithers path per lane, launched concurrently
- an injected collision-provider adapter that reuses workspace-service plumbing without adding a GitHub client, task store, or runner
- exact legacy fallback for planner failures and unscoped single-task plans

## What kind of change is this?

Feature, non-breaking and default OFF.

# Documentation changes needed?

No user-facing documentation change is required for this independently landable W1. The setting is exported in code and defaults OFF while the broader #16443 orchestration stack is assembled.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

- `plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/lane-planner.ts`
- `plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/actions/tasks.ts`
- `plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/__tests__/lane-planner.test.ts`

## Detailed testing steps

```bash
cd /tmp
bun test /path/to/eliza/plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/__tests__/lane-planner.test.ts
```

Result after rebase: **14 pass, 0 fail, 57 expectations**.

Covered behaviors include decomposition, overlap/cap rejection, PR collision annotation, difficulty-tag contract, gate OFF/ON, concurrent lane startup, one durable create path per lane, metadata wave stamping, unscoped legacy behavior, planning fallback, content-agent de-duplication, and no legacy replay after execution begins.

  plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/index.ts \

Codex reviewed the uncommitted patch repeatedly. All reported findings were fixed, including content-agent duplication, unscoped prompt safety, lane-cap truncation, execution replay, concurrent execution, and settled-result type narrowing.

topPRs.title: feat(orchestrator): supervise wave lane lifecycle (W3 of #16443)
topPRs.author: 0xSolace
topPRs.body:
## Summary

W3 of #16443. Adds a default-off `WaveSupervisor` to `plugin-agent-orchestrator` for wave-scoped lane lifecycle management.

- reads the canonical `metadata.waveId` contract, with defensive aliases for manually stamped tasks
- refills terminal lanes while the wave goal remains unmet through an injected `WaveRefillPlanner` interface
- ships a no-op planner fallback so W3 can land before W1; W1 can register `ORCHESTRATOR_LANE_PLANNER` with the same interface without changing W3
- detects failed-lane uncommitted work via `git status`, preserves lifecycle-registered workspaces, and includes the preserved path/files in replacement metadata and brief
- re-checks active lane scopes against sibling scopes and matching-repository open PR changed files, warning once per collision pair in the originating room
- layers a per-wave concurrency reservation/cap over the existing durable admission queue, including head-of-line avoidance across waves
- persists compact wave status in existing task metadata and surfaces it through `ACTIVE_SUB_AGENTS`
- gates all behavior behind `ELIZA_ORCHESTRATOR_WAVE_SUPERVISOR` (default OFF)

## Redundancy check and design choice

I read the existing watchdog, reflexion/respawn path, task service/store/types, admission queue, Smithers integration, active-sub-agent provider, workspace lifecycle/registry, and swarm coordinator before implementation.

This is a **new service rather than an extension of `TaskWatchdogService`**. The watchdog is session-liveness detection and reminder delivery; wave supervision owns a different aggregate lifecycle plus admission control and planner orchestration. Combining them would couple default-on watchdog behavior to a default-off feature and expand the watchdog's responsibilities substantially. W3 does reuse its proven structure: pure detectors, one tick owner, in-memory one-time warning keys, target resolution through the task service, no new store, and timer-free policy tests.

Existing mechanisms reused:

- task durability and metadata: `OrchestratorTaskService` / existing store
- dispatch backpressure: existing admission queue and its durable admission record
- salvage ownership: workspace lifecycle plus shared registry, without adopting caller-owned paths
- status visibility: existing `ACTIVE_SUB_AGENTS` provider
- retry context remains owned by existing reflexion/respawn logic

## Configuration

- `ELIZA_ORCHESTRATOR_WAVE_SUPERVISOR=true` enables the service
- `ELIZA_ORCHESTRATOR_WAVE_CONCURRENCY=<n>` sets the default per-wave cap (default 4)
- `ELIZA_ORCHESTRATOR_WAVE_INTERVAL_MS=<ms>` sets tick cadence (minimum 5000, default 60000)
- task metadata `waveConcurrencyCap` overrides the default for that wave

## Evidence

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| authoritative per-file unit test | `bun test plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/__tests__/wave-supervisor.test.ts` | PASS, 6 tests / 18 assertions |
| targeted Vitest suite | `bunx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/__tests__/wave-supervisor.test.ts src/__tests__/admission-queue.test.ts src/__tests__/admission-integration.test.ts` | PASS, 3 files / 26 tests |
| formatting/lint | `bunx @biomejs/biome check <six changed files>` | PASS |
| patch hygiene | `git diff --check` | PASS |
| package typecheck | `bun run typecheck` | BLOCKED by existing workspace/dependency failures outside W3 (`reset-soonest` generated contract mismatch plus missing `ai`, `markdown-it`, `file-type`, and `fast-redact` declarations); no W3-file diagnostic emitted |
| review | `codex review --uncommitted` (two passes) | Findings fixed: queue reservation releases, degraded-recording release, and repository-qualified PR collision matching |

## Scope

No new store or UI. No W1/W2 planner/create-path/completion-evidence changes. No lockfile, Vite config, or binary changes.
